Forward-facing, or the direction straight ahead

meaning_arabic: الفارغ المنتهي من عمله غير المشغول والمتفرغ
question: What does the Hassaniya word “صَايِبْ” mean?
options: Busy and preoccupied while completing one's work
Free and unoccupied after finishing one's work
Tired and resting before returning to one's work
Ready and prepared before beginning one's work

meaning_arabic: المشغول بأمر أو مشكلة تشغله مكرها بغير راحة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “وَاحِلْ” mean?
options: Occupied with a pleasant task that keeps one willingly engaged
Free from any concern and able to rest without interruption
Preoccupied by a problem or matter that keeps one unwillingly busy
Focused on a chosen task that demands steady concentration

meaning_arabic: البادئ الشارع في الأمر والعمل من أوله
question: What does the Hassaniya word “إِمْسَنْتِي” mean?
options: Someone resuming a task after leaving it unfinished
Someone abandoning a matter or task before its completion
Someone completing a matter or task after prolonged work
Someone beginning a matter or task from its start

meaning_arabic: المنتهي المتفرغ بعد فراغه من عمل كان منشغلا به
question: What does the Hassaniya word “وَافِي” mean?
options: Someone free after finishing work that had occupied them
Someone interrupting work because another task has arisen
Someone preparing to begin work after a period of rest
Someone remaining busy with work that is nearly completed

meaning_arabic: السريع الحثيث السير أو سريع البديهة والفهم
question: What does the Hassaniya word “سَابِگْ” mean?
options: Slow and deliberate in movement, or cautious in understanding
Fast and brisk in movement, or quick-witted in understanding
Steady and tireless in movement, or patient in understanding
Erratic and restless in movement, or uncertain in understanding

meaning_arabic: البطيء المتثاقل في مشيه وسيره ونحو ذلك
question: What does the Hassaniya word “رَابِي” mean?
options: Light and effortless in walking or movement
Fast and energetic in walking or movement
Slow and heavy in walking or movement
Unsteady and irregular in walking or movement

meaning_arabic: الكريم السخي في معاملته أو الشيء المفيد النافع
question: What does the Hassaniya word “مَعْلُومْ” mean?
options: Strict and demanding in one's dealings, or something difficult and troublesome
Careful and restrained in one's dealings, or something ordinary and familiar
Reserved and cautious in one's dealings, or something scarce and valuable
Generous and giving in one's dealings, or something useful and beneficial

meaning_arabic: البخيل الممسك لماله المانع رفده عن الناس
question: What does the Hassaniya word “مَرْخُوسْ” mean?
options: A stingy person who withholds wealth and assistance from others
A prudent person who carefully manages wealth for others
A generous person who readily shares wealth with others
A wealthy person who openly displays possessions before others

meaning_arabic: الغالي في الثمن أو الصعب الشديد الوعورة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “وَاعِرْ” mean?
options: Cheap in price, or easy and pleasantly smooth
Expensive in price, or difficult and extremely rough
Moderate in price, or ordinary and fairly manageable
Uncertain in price, or changing and highly unpredictable

meaning_arabic: الرخيص الزهيد الثمن أو السهل اللين
question: What does the Hassaniya word “هَيِّنْ” mean?
options: Costly and expensive, or difficult and demanding
Rare and valuable, or delicate and fragile
Cheap and inexpensive, or easy and gentle
Common and abundant, or ordinary and familiar

meaning_arabic: المرتفع الصاعد في مكان عال أو الشيء العالي
question: What does the Hassaniya word “رَاگِبْ” mean?
options: Level or extending across flat ground
Descending or situated on a downward slope
Hidden or situated behind another object
Elevated or rising in a high place

meaning_arabic: المنخفض الهابط في وهدة أو مكان واطئ من الأرض
question: What does the Hassaniya word “گَاظُّ” mean?
options: Low and descending into a hollow or low-lying place
Level and extending across a flat part of the land
Elevated and rising on a high part of the land
Narrow and confined between two raised parts of the land

meaning_arabic: صغير الإبل منذ ولادته إلى مقاربة السنة وملازمته أمه
question: What does the Hassaniya word “إِحْوَارْ” mean?
options: A young camel from one to two years old, beginning to separate from its mother
A young camel from birth until nearly one year old, remaining close to its mother
A young camel from two to three years old, becoming largely independent of its mother
A young camel from three to four years old, no longer dependent on its mother

meaning_arabic: ولد الناقة إذا قارب السنة وأصبحت أمه عُشراء من جديد
question: What does the Hassaniya word “اِبْنِ اعْشَارْ” mean?
options: A camel calf nearing two years old when its mother has just weaned it
A camel calf nearing three years old when its mother leaves it behind
A camel calf nearing one year old when its mother becomes pregnant again
A camel calf nearing four years old when its mother stops nursing entirely

meaning_arabic: ولد الناقة في عمر سنة إلى سنة ونصف حين يشتد ويقوى
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أگْعَسْ” mean?
options: A camel calf from birth to one year, while still weak and dependent
A camel calf from two to three years, when it begins living independently
A camel calf from one and a half to two years, when it is newly weaned
A camel calf from one to one and a half years, when it becomes stronger

meaning_arabic: ولد الناقة المفطوم بعد سنة ونصف إذا وضعت أمه حوارا بعده
question: What does the Hassaniya word “بِلْبُونْ” mean?
options: A camel calf weaned after a year and a half when its mother gives birth to another calf
A camel calf approaching one year while remaining constantly beside its mother
A camel calf still nursing after one year because its mother has not conceived again
A camel calf over two years that has begun living independently of its mother

meaning_arabic: ولد الناقة في سن سنتين إلى ثلاث عند بداية استقلاله عن أمه
question: What does the Hassaniya word “آمْسَخْسِرْ” mean?
options: A young camel aged one to two years, still remaining closely dependent on its mother
A young camel aged two to three years, beginning to become independent of its mother
A young camel aged three to four years, already fully independent of its mother
A young camel aged four to five years, beginning to be trained for heavy work

meaning_arabic: ولد الناقة إذا أكمل ثلاث سنوات ودخل في السنة الرابعة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “حِگّْ” mean?
options: A young camel that has completed two years and entered its third
A young camel that has completed four years and entered its fifth
A young camel that has completed three years and entered its fourth
A young camel that has completed five years and entered its sixth

meaning_arabic: البعير الذي قارب السنة الخامسة من عمره، أو المراهق من الفتيان
question: What does the Hassaniya word “اجْدَعْ” mean?
options: A camel nearing its third year, or a very young child
A camel nearing its fourth year, or a fully grown man
A camel nearing its sixth year, or an elderly man
A camel nearing its fifth year, or an adolescent boy

meaning_arabic: البعير الذي أتم السنة الخامسة وبدأ السادسة؛ ويعني كذلك الذلول المروّض المنقاد للركوب والحمل.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أَدَارِيفْ” mean?
options: A camel that has completed five years and entered its sixth; also a docile trained camel for riding or carrying loads
A camel that has completed six years and entered its seventh; also one reserved only for breeding
A camel that has completed four years and entered its fifth; also one still untrained for riding
A camel that has completed seven years and entered its eighth; also one too old for riding or carrying loads

meaning_arabic: البعير الذي طعن في سنته السادسة وسقطت ثنيته اللبنية
question: What does the Hassaniya word “إِثْنِي” mean?
options: A camel that has entered its seventh year and shed its next milk incisors
A camel that has entered its sixth year and shed its first milk incisors
A camel that has entered its eighth year and shed a later set of milk incisors
A camel that has entered its ninth year and completed its permanent dentition

meaning_arabic: البعير الذي طعن في سنته السابعة وسقطت رباعيته اللبنية
question: What does the Hassaniya word “ارْبَاعْ” mean?
options: A camel that has entered its sixth year and shed its first milk incisors
A camel that has entered its eighth year and shed the following milk incisors
A camel that has entered its seventh year and shed its second pair of milk incisors
A camel that has entered its ninth year and completed its adult teeth

meaning_arabic: البعير الذي طعن في سنته الثامنة وسقط سنه بعد الرباعية
question: What does the Hassaniya word “إِسْدَاسْ” mean?
options: A camel that has entered its seventh year and shed the tooth before the rubāʿiyya
A camel that has entered its tenth year and begun wearing down its incisors
A camel that has entered its ninth year and begun losing its canine tooth
A camel that has entered its eighth year and shed the tooth following the rubāʿiyya

meaning_arabic: البعير الذي طعن في سنته التاسعة وشق نابه واكتملت أسنانه
question: What does the Hassaniya word “فَاطِرْ” mean?
options: A camel in its ninth year whose canine has emerged and whose teeth are complete
A camel in its eighth year whose later milk incisors have fallen out
A camel in its seventh year whose first adult incisors have appeared
A camel in its tenth year whose teeth have begun visibly wearing down

meaning_arabic: البعير الذي اكتملت أسنانه منذ سنتين وبلغ إحدى عشرة سنة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “إِمْكَرَّرْ الْفَطْرَه” mean?
options: A ten-year-old camel whose teeth have been complete for one year
An eleven-year-old camel whose teeth have been complete for two years
A twelve-year-old camel whose teeth have begun losing their ridges
A thirteen-year-old camel whose canine has begun showing heavy wear

meaning_arabic: البعير في السنة الثانية عشرة حين تبدأ تموجات أسنانه تختفي
question: What does the Hassaniya word “مَاسَحْ اشْرُكْ” mean?
options: A camel in its eleventh year, when its permanent teeth finish emerging
A camel in its thirteenth year, when its canine tooth begins breaking
A camel in its twelfth year, when the ridges of its teeth begin disappearing
A camel beyond thirteen years, when obvious signs of old age appear

meaning_arabic: البعير الذي بلغ سن الثالثة عشرة من عمره تماما
question: What does the Hassaniya word “سَالِخْ النَّابْ” mean?
options: A camel that has reached exactly eleven years of age
A camel that has reached exactly twelve years of age
A camel that has passed beyond thirteen years of age
A camel that has reached exactly thirteen years of age

meaning_arabic: البعير الذي تجاوز الثالثة عشرة وبدأت تظهر عليه علامات الكبر
question: What does the Hassaniya word “عَوْدْ” mean?
options: A camel older than thirteen years and beginning to show signs of aging
A camel exactly thirteen years old whose teeth have just become complete
A camel nearing thirteen years but still showing no signs of aging
A camel about twelve years old whose tooth ridges are beginning to fade

meaning_arabic: الذكر من الإبل في ركوبه إذا كان سنه بين ابن اعشار واجدع
question: What does the Hassaniya word “إِبْعِيرْ” mean?
options: A male camel used for breeding between the higg and ithni stages
A male camel used for riding between the ibn ʿashār and ajdaʿ stages
A female camel used for riding between the ajdaʿ and ithni stages
A male camel used for carrying loads between the fatir and awd stages

meaning_arabic: الصغير من ذكور الإبل إذا بلغ مرحلة أمسخسر حتى أداريف
question: What does the Hassaniya word “كِرْژِي” mean?
options: A young female camel from the amsakhser stage through the adarif stage
A young male camel from the hiwar stage through the ibn ʿashār stage
A young male camel from the amsakhser stage through the adarif stage
A mature male camel from the ithni stage through the fatir stage

meaning_arabic: الذكر من الإبل في الركوب إذا كان سنه بين المخلول والحِگ
question: What does the Hassaniya word “الْحَاشِي” mean?
options: A female camel used for riding between the makhlul and higg stages
A male camel used for breeding between the ajdaʿ and ithni stages
A male camel used for carrying loads between the higg and fatir stages
A male camel used for riding between the makhlul and higg stages

meaning_arabic: الجمل في الركوب إذا كان سنه في مرحلة ما بين اجدع وإثني
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أَوْصِرَاطْ” mean?
options: A riding camel whose age falls between the ajdaʿ and ithni stages
A breeding camel whose age falls between the ithni and fatir stages
A riding camel whose age falls between the higg and ajdaʿ stages
A pack camel whose age falls between the fatir and awd stages

meaning_arabic: أنثى الإبل التي تقابل أوصراط في سنها ورُوّضت للركوب
question: What does the Hassaniya word “الصَّيْدَحْ” mean?
options: A female camel matching a fatir in age and kept only for breeding
A female camel matching an awsirat in age and trained for riding
A male camel matching an awsirat in age and trained for carrying loads
A female camel matching a higg in age and still untrained for riding

meaning_arabic: الجمل الضخم الذي يكون غالبا فحل الإبل ورئيسها ولا يُركب
question: What does the Hassaniya word “آگْعُودْ” mean?
options: A small camel usually kept as a young riding animal and rarely used for breeding
A mature camel usually trained for carrying loads and regularly ridden on journeys
A huge camel usually serving as breeding male and herd leader and not ridden
A lean camel usually kept apart from the herd and used mainly for racing

meaning_arabic: المشي البطيء أي الدبيب لذوات الأرجل ومنها سير الإبل
question: What does the Hassaniya word “نَّگَوْطَرْ” mean?
options: To move at a brisk walking pace, including the gait of camels
To move at a fast running pace, including the gait of camels
To move at a steady trotting pace, including the gait of camels
To move with a slow creeping walk, including the gait of camels

meaning_arabic: التزيّد وهو أول مراحل الانطلاق من المشي إلى العدو
question: What does the Hassaniya word “يِتْرَگْ” mean?
options: To accelerate in the first stage of moving from a walk toward a run
To decelerate in the first stage of moving from a run toward a walk
To settle into a steady pace after completing a transition into a run
To stop briefly before beginning a transition from standing into a walk

meaning_arabic: الخَبَب وهو ضرب سريع من العدو يحمل قوة وقدرة عليه
question: What does the Hassaniya word “يْلَگْلَگْ” mean?
options: A slow walking gait performed with caution and little exertion
A fast trotting gait performed with strength and capability
A steady pacing gait performed with balance and restrained effort
A short stopping gait performed after prolonged and tiring movement

meaning_arabic: السير الشديد الذي يؤثر بالأرض ويقابل الرسيم باللغة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “يْسَيَّرْ” mean?
options: A light gait that barely touches the ground and corresponds to a gentle walk
A slow gait that drags along the ground and corresponds to creeping movement
A forceful gait that leaves an effect on the ground, corresponding to rasīm
A leaping gait that repeatedly clears the ground and corresponds to bounding

meaning_arabic: سير يقدّم فيه البعير عنقه ويمدّه ويقابل العَسْج باللغة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “يُسَنِّفْ” mean?
options: A camel gait in which it lowers and retracts its neck, corresponding to a crouching gait
A camel gait in which it swings its neck sideways, corresponding to a swaying gait
A camel gait in which it raises its neck upright, corresponding to a high-stepping gait
A camel gait in which it extends its neck forward, corresponding to ʿasj

meaning_arabic: المشي السريع جدا الذي يطابق سيره الوَسْج عند العرب
question: What does the Hassaniya word “يَگْرُنْ” mean?
options: An extremely fast walk corresponding to the gait called wasj
A slow deliberate walk corresponding to the gait called dabīb
A steady moderate walk corresponding to the gait called rasīm
A bounding running gait corresponding to the gait called khabab

meaning_arabic: أشدّ عدو وسرعة للإبل بحيث تضرب فيه بقوائمها الأربع معا
question: What does the Hassaniya word “يَرْبَعْ” mean?
options: A slow camel gait in which the legs move in alternating pairs
The fastest camel run, with all four legs striking together
A moderate camel run in which each leg strikes the ground separately
A steady camel trot in which the forelegs strike before the hind legs

meaning_arabic: الراكب الجملَ مُرَحَّلاً وهو للإبل كالفارس للخيل
question: What does the Hassaniya word “إِبْجَاوِي” mean?
options: A handler leading a loaded camel, comparable to a groom with horses
A breeder tending a camel herd, comparable to a stableman with horses
A rider mounted on a saddled camel, comparable to a horseman on horseback
A driver guiding a pack camel, comparable to a coachman with horses

meaning_arabic: مَرْكَبُ الرَّجُلِ على البعير بلوازمه أو مفرداً
question: What does the Hassaniya word “الرَّاحْلَه” mean?
options: A camel's tethering gear, with its ropes or by itself
A woman's camel litter, with its coverings or by itself
A camel's pack frame, with its loads or by itself
A man's camel saddle, with its fittings or by itself

meaning_arabic: الجزء الأمامي ومُقَدَّم الراحلة الذي يقع بين فخذي الراكب
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أگْرْبُوصْ” mean?
options: The front part of a camel saddle positioned between the rider's thighs
The lower part of a camel saddle resting directly on the camel's spine
The rear part of a camel saddle positioned behind the rider's back
The side part of a camel saddle positioned beside the rider's knees

meaning_arabic: اللوحان الخشبيان اللذان يكوّنان ميمنة وميسرة الراحلة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “اِصْفِفْ الرَّاحْلَه” mean?
options: The two leather straps forming the front and rear of the camel saddle
The two wooden boards forming the right and left sides of the camel saddle
The two padded cushions forming the upper and lower parts of the camel saddle
The two rope loops forming the inner and outer parts of the camel saddle

meaning_arabic: اللوح الخلفي للراحلة عند ظهر الراكب الذي يستند إليه
question: What does the Hassaniya word “تَانْتْفَارْتْ” mean?
options: The lower board of the camel saddle beneath the rider, used as a base
The front board of the camel saddle before the rider, used as a handhold
The rear board of the camel saddle behind the rider, used as a backrest
The side board of the camel saddle beside the rider, used as a support

meaning_arabic: الدعامتان الخشبيتان المثبتتان عن يمين وشمال الراحلة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “لِمْرَاشِيكْ” mean?
options: Two leather straps fixed at the front and rear of the camel saddle
Two rope loops fixed beneath the camel saddle for tying loads
Two padded supports fixed above and below the camel saddle
Two wooden supports fixed to the right and left of the camel saddle

meaning_arabic: الجزآن السفليان من الراحلة اللذان يلامسان ظهر البعير
question: What does the Hassaniya word “الْغِرْبَانْ” mean?
options: The two lower parts of the camel saddle that touch the camel's back
The two upper parts of the camel saddle that support the rider's thighs
The two front parts of the camel saddle that secure the rider's hands
The two rear parts of the camel saddle that support the rider's back

meaning_arabic: الفرشة المصنوعة تحت رحل البعير وتسمى عند العرب الحِلْس
question: What does the Hassaniya word “اللِّبْدَه” mean?
options: The cover placed above a camel saddle, called kisāʾ in Arabic
The pad placed beneath a camel saddle, called ḥils in Arabic
The strap fastened around a camel saddle, called ḥizām in Arabic
The board fitted behind a camel saddle, called muʾakhkhara in Arabic

meaning_arabic: الحلقات الدائرية المثبتة بأسفل مقاعد الراحلة لربط الحبال
question: What does the Hassaniya word “لِحْلَاگْ” mean?
options: Wooden pegs fixed beneath the saddle seats for supporting boards
Leather straps fixed beneath the saddle seats for securing cushions
Round rings fixed beneath the saddle seats for tying ropes
Padded loops fixed beneath the saddle seats for protecting the camel

meaning_arabic: الحبل المفتول المشدود تحت صدر الجمل لتثبيت رحله وغاربه
question: What does the Hassaniya word “الْغِرْظَه” mean?
options: A twisted rope tightened beneath the camel's belly to secure its load and packs
A twisted rope tightened behind the camel's rump to secure its saddle and tailpiece
A twisted rope tightened around the camel's neck to secure its reins and halter
A twisted rope tightened beneath the camel's chest to secure its saddle and withers

meaning_arabic: حبل غليظ مفتول من سيور الجلد يثبت الراحلة ويسمى الحَقَب
question: What does the Hassaniya word “آسْفِلْ” mean?
options: A thick braided rope of leather strips used to secure the camel saddle
A thin woven rope of wool used to decorate the camel saddle
A broad padded strap of cloth used to cushion the camel saddle
A narrow twisted cord of hair used to attach the camel reins

meaning_arabic: فرش الراحلة المصنوع من جلد ضأن مدبوغ مع صوفه ويصلى عليه
question: What does the Hassaniya word “تْلِوِيشْ” mean?
options: Camel-saddle bedding made from tanned goatskin without hair and used as a sleeping mat
Camel-saddle bedding made from tanned sheepskin with its wool and used for prayer
Camel-saddle bedding made from woven wool and used as a covering at night
Camel-saddle bedding made from woven leather strips and used beneath baggage

meaning_arabic: الهودج المُقَبَّب بثوب فوق الجمل تركب فيه المرأة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “حِجْبَه” mean?
options: A camel litter enclosed at the sides but left uncovered above for a woman to ride in
A camel saddle fitted with wooden sideboards for a man to ride on
A camel litter arched with cloth above the camel for a woman to ride in
A camel pack frame covered with cloth for carrying household goods

meaning_arabic: الهودج المحَفَّف غير المقبَّب بثوب فوق الجمل
question: What does the Hassaniya word “جِحْفَه” mean?
options: A camel pack frame wrapped in cloth for protecting provisions
A camel litter arched over with cloth and fully enclosed above
A camel saddle framed with wood but left open on both sides
A camel litter surrounded with cloth but not arched over with it

meaning_arabic: الغَبِيط الخشبي المركب تحت الهودج على ظهر الناقة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “لِخْرَجْ” mean?
options: The wooden frame mounted beneath a litter on the she-camel's back
The padded mat placed above a litter to support its cloth covering
The leather girth tightened beneath a litter around the she-camel's chest
The cloth canopy stretched above a litter to shade the woman riding inside

meaning_arabic: دعامتان محشوتان بالأعشاب على جانبي لخرج لنصب الهودج
question: What does the Hassaniya word “التِّيزِيَّاتِنْ” mean?
options: Two wooden poles tied behind the litter frame for hanging baggage
Two grass-stuffed supports on either side of the frame for setting up the litter
Two leather straps stretched beneath the litter frame for securing it
Two cloth cushions placed above the litter frame for seating the rider

meaning_arabic: الهودج الذي لا يصلح لأن يقبب بل يُحَفّ بثوب كالمحفّة
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أَرَحَّالْ” mean?
options: A litter too narrow for cloth covering and instead fitted with wooden sides
A litter suitable for an arched canopy and completely covered with leather
A litter unsuitable for an arched canopy and instead surrounded with cloth
A litter too heavy for riding and instead used for carrying household goods

meaning_arabic: حِمْل الجمل المكوَّن من الخيمة المطوية ومتاع أهلها
question: What does the Hassaniya word “التُّوظِيتْ” mean?
options: A camel load consisting of grain sacks and water containers
A camel load consisting of firewood and cooking equipment
A camel load consisting of trading goods and market provisions
A camel load consisting of a folded tent and the family's belongings

meaning_arabic: الإنسان أو الآدمي ذكراً كان أو أنثى صغيراً أو كبيراً
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أَرْگَاجْ” mean?
options: A human being, male or female, young or old
An adult person, male or female, but not a child
A male person, young or old, but not a female

A mass of hardened sandy deposits attached to tree trunks, resembling a howdah on an animal

Dust and sand left behind after seasonal flooding
Dust and sand raised into the air by the wind

Broad channels on plains formed by repeated sheet flooding

A strip beside a wadi forming a terrace or level above the channel
A strip within a wadi forming a sandy bed below the banks

Channel flow cutting through a steep slope, later used as a term for that valley form

The mouth and outlet of a wadi

Shallow channels left by gentle runoff
Deep gullies left by powerful floodwater
Narrow ridges left by deposited sediment

A flat area forming a ridge between two valleys
A flat area forming a basin below several highlands
A flat area forming an opening or gap between two highlands

question: What does the Hassaniya word “احْسَيَّات” mean?

Small pits or wells three or four meters deep near wadis that remain permanently full

question: What does the Hassaniya word “إوني” mean?

Building barriers of earth and stone around a tent to protect it from floodwater
Building barriers of sand and cloth around a tent to protect it from drifting dunes

question: What does the Hassaniya word “مَرْوَحْ” mean?

A medium-distance unit equal to what an ordinary camel covers in half a day, up to about 20 kilometers
A long-distance unit equal to what an ordinary camel covers in a full day, up to about 40 kilometers

The distance a camel covers in half a day at a normal walk without trotting

A travel stage normally covered in half a day at an ordinary pace
A travel stage typically covered after sunset during the cooler hours

question: What does the Hassaniya word “مَسْتَدْبِي” mean?

A medium journey requiring departure at sunrise, travel through the afternoon, and arrival before nightfall
A night journey requiring departure after sunset, travel until dawn, and no overnight stop midway

The distance covered in one third of a day
The distance covered in a full day

A heavy metal bowl with a handle used for serving food after cooking

meaning_arabic: السرج ولوازمه.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أَشِرْمَاطْ” mean?
options: The reins and their fittings
The load and its containers
The saddle and its equipment
The tether and its ropes

meaning_arabic: ناقة لقحة تروي حوارها الذي هو من أب كريم أصيل.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “لَگْحَه تروي وِلّ اِمْشَوَّطْ” mean?
options: A she-camel that carries a calf descended from a strong and fast sire
A she-camel that protects a calf descended from a large and healthy sire
A she-camel that leads a calf descended from a trained and obedient sire
A she-camel that gives ample milk to her calf, which is sired by a noble purebred male

meaning_arabic: الحوار الذي يولد في الصيف، ويكون في العادة صغير الحجم.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “مَژُوژْ” mean?
options: A camel calf born in summer and usually small in size
A camel calf born in winter and usually heavy in size
A camel calf born in spring and usually tall in size
A camel calf born in autumn and usually broad in size

meaning_arabic: الحوار السمين المكعّر الذي يحمل في سنامه شحمًا.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أَبُلَايْ” mean?
options: A lean camel calf with a flat back and little fat
A fat, rounded camel calf carrying fat in its hump
A tall camel calf with long legs and a narrow body
A young camel calf with thick hair and a broad chest

meaning_arabic: اللبن الجديد الذي يأتي بعد اللبإ؛ ويسمى أيضًا «اللّْبَنْ لِمْجِدّْ» و«اللّْبَنْ الْعَاگْبْ الصَّرْبَه».
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أَمَصَّاطْ” mean?
options: The first colostrum produced immediately after birth
The sour milk produced after fresh milk has fermented
The fresh milk that comes after the colostrum
The thick milk remaining after butter has been churned

meaning_arabic: كثير الحركة واللعب الزائد.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “اِمْحَبْرَطْ” mean?
options: Very quiet and inclined to remain still
Very stubborn and inclined to resist others
Very talkative and inclined to interrupt others
Very restless and excessively playful

meaning_arabic: كثرة الحركة واللعب الزائد.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “اِلتّْحَبْرِيطْ” mean?
options: Excessive movement and playfulness
Excessive talking and joking
Excessive eating and drinking
Excessive sleeping and idleness

meaning_arabic: ما يُقدَّم للضيوف قبل الوجبة الرئيسة لفتح الشهية؛ ويُستعمل أيضًا لكل ما يحفّز الشخص على أداء عمل أو الإقدام على أمر وإنجازه راغبًا.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أَمَظَّايْ” mean?
options: A drink served after the main meal, or anything that helps a person relax after completing a task
An appetizer offered before the main meal, or anything that motivates a person to undertake and complete a task willingly
A gift presented during the main meal, or anything that rewards a person after successfully finishing a task
A snack carried between meals, or anything that distracts a person while postponing a difficult task

meaning_arabic: الطعام.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “اِلظّْوَاگْ” mean?
options: Drink
Clothing
Food
Shelter

meaning_arabic: أتطفل.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “نِتصَّگَّطْ” mean?
options: I withdraw
I hesitate
I complain
I intrude

meaning_arabic: أطراف الشاة التي يتكوّن منها الشواء المقدّم أولًا للضيف.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “أَفَشَايْ” mean?
options: The sheep extremities used to make the roast served first to a guest
The sheep ribs used to make the stew served last to a guest
The sheep organs used to make the broth served first to a guest
The sheep shoulder used to make the roast served last to a guest

meaning_arabic: الوعد الصادق الموثوق، أو الالتزام بوعد ذي مصداقية.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “تَانِكْفِرْتْ / تَنَكْفَارْتْ” mean?
options: A tentative promise whose fulfillment remains uncertain
A sincere, trustworthy promise or a credible commitment
A public promise made mainly to impress other people
A conditional promise dependent on receiving something first

meaning_arabic: يرقص نوعًا من الرَّديح عند سماع الطرب.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “يِرْكِسْ” mean?
options: To sing a type of rhythmic chant on hearing pleasing music
To clap a type of rhythmic pattern on hearing pleasing music
To dance a type of radih on hearing pleasing music
To recite a type of rhythmic poetry on hearing pleasing music

meaning_arabic: رجل مهمل غير محتاط، متهاون في شؤونه.
question: What does the Hassaniya word “المنفوش” mean?
options: A man who is strict, cautious, and meticulous in his affairs
A man who is timid, hesitant, and withdrawn in his affairs
A man who is restless, impatient, and hurried in his affairs
A man who is careless, incautious, and negligent in his affairs
